title: Using AI to Simulate the Behaviour of European Populations
abstract: arXiv:2611.33503v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models can stand in for survey respondents, but leading approaches build their simulated people from interviews or individual records. We show that a model can learn how European population groups respond from published statistics, without interviews and without training on individual records. We fine-tune an open-weight language model on more than 12 million published group-level answer distributions from about 40 European countries, setting it up to predict each group's departure from a reference distribution. On opinion surveys from its training families it calls the direction of group differences right 84% of the time, ahead of a demographic statistical model (77%, paired test) and level with Claude Opus 5 and 5.5, which it also ties on accuracy; the frontier models are more accurate on new questions. translated_title: 用人工智能模拟欧洲人群的行为
translated_abstract: 语言模型可以替代调查受访者，但主流方法是通过访谈或个人记录来构建模拟的人。我们证明，一个模型可以仅从公开的统计数据中学习欧洲人群组的反应方式，无需访谈，也无需在个人记录上训练。我们在来自约40个欧洲国家的超过1200万条已发表的群体层面答案分布上微调了一个开源权重语言模型，使其能够预测每个群体相对于参考分布的偏离情况。在其训练所属调查家族的民意调查中，它在84%的情况下正确判断群体差异的方向，优于一个人口统计模型（77%，配对检验），并与Claude Opus 5和5.5持平，在准确率上也与后者打平；前沿模型在新问题上更准确。在278个留出问题上（几乎全部来自训练时见过的调查家族），其误差比该统计模型低12%。
tldr: 该研究仅需在约40个欧洲国家公开的1200多万条群体级调查答案分布上微调开源语言模型，无需访谈或个人数据即可模拟欧洲人群的调查反应，判断群体差异方向的准确率达84%，超越传统人口统计模型并与Claude Opus等前沿大模型持平。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that fine-tuning an open-weight language model on over 12 million published group-level survey answer distributions from ~40 European countries enables accurate simulation of population responses without interviews or individual records, achieving 84% accuracy in predicting group difference directions—outperforming demographic statistical models and matching frontier models like Claude Opus 5 and 5.5.
